sprint: Image Studio Ship D — Crop Sub-Panel: Trash It + Keep This (Both Options Required). Direct product request (verbatim, with an attached screenshot of the intended crop sub-panel showing a pink 'Trash It' button, a teal 'Keep This' button, and an 'Undo Trim' action): 'check this for trim functionality. this is what we need. trash it and keep it both options are required.' Both trash and keep are mathematical duals operating on the same selection box: Keep This crops the working buffer to the box's contents (keeps only inside, shrinks dimensions); Trash It clears every pixel inside the box to fully transparent (removes only inside, dimensions preserved). Undo Trim reverts either op via the shared `_preCropSnapshot`. **Data-model side, in `js/pictureStudio.js`**: a new pure function `_trashPixelsInBox(pb,bounds)` sits alongside the pre-existing `_cropPixelBuffer(pb,bounds)` — same signature shape but writes RGBA `(0,0,0,0)` inside the bounds instead of extracting a smaller sub-buffer, returning a genuinely new `Uint8ClampedArray` (never mutating the input, verified). A new `_cropTrashBtn` module-level variable joins the existing `_cropApplyBtn`/`_cropResetBtn` `let` declaration. **UI-side rewrite of `_buildCropSubPanel()`**: hint text changed from 'Drag on the picture to pick a crop area, then Apply.' to 'Drag a box around a part of your picture.' (matching the reference screenshot's own wording, and framing the action row below as two peer choices rather than one Apply step). The action row's two buttons render in left→right order Trash It → Keep This, deliberately with Trash It first because 'get rid of this part' is the more common gesture on a real photo per the reference sheet's own layout. Trash It carries `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn picture-studio-subpanel-btn-danger` (a genuinely filled coral pill, not the old subtle outline — see CSS update below), text '🗑 Trash It', click handler `_trashCropArea`. Keep This carries `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn picture-studio-subpanel-btn-primary` (unchanged gold pill CTA), text '✓ Keep This' (renamed from '✂️ Apply Crop'), click handler `_applyCrop` unchanged. Undo Trim is a full-width smaller pill beneath the row (`.picture-studio-subpanel-btn-sm`), text '↩ Undo Trim' (renamed from '↩ Reset Crop'), click handler `_resetCrop` unchanged — honestly describes what happens regardless of which op ran, since `_preCropSnapshot` backs both. Auto Crop to Content is unchanged, still sits below Undo Trim. **New `_trashCropArea()` handler**: mirrors `_applyCrop()`'s exact clamp math, `_preCropSnapshot` capture pattern, and stroke-history clear, but calls `_trashPixelsInBox` instead of `_cropPixelBuffer` and deliberately does NOT reset pan/beforeAfter/BA-slider state — since buffer dimensions are unchanged after trash, all prior compare/pan state is still meaningful (matching how the pre-existing `_applyCrop` explicitly recenters BECAUSE dimensions change). Stroke history IS cleared for safety, matching Keep This's own clear-history rule (so a later undo can never restore a stroke that painted where content is now deliberately gone). **`_refreshBgControls`** disabled-state sync now toggles all three buttons together: Keep This/Trash It disabled when no `_cropRect` OR no `_bgRemovedImg`; Undo Trim disabled when no `_preCropSnapshot` (unchanged). **CSS update in `css/style.css`**: `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn-danger` upgraded from a subtle outline (color:#C0392B, transparent background, translucent border) to a genuinely filled coral pill (color:#FFFFFF, background:#E67373, border-color:#D96565, font-weight:700, hover:#DC6060) matching the reference screenshot's stronger visual weight — Trash It is a destructive action, should read as heavier weight than Keep This's constructive gold CTA, and the two colours signal opposite intents within one shared action row. Docstring above the rule explains the reasoning.
task: Verified end-to-end via a new 19-assertion Playwright suite (scratch-only, `trash_keep_verify.js`) split into two parts: **Part 2 (pure-function pixel logic, 4/4)** — copies `_trashPixelsInBox` verbatim and exercises it against a real 4×4 fully-opaque red `Uint8ClampedArray` with a 2×2 box at (1,1). Confirms trashed buffer dimensions preserved (4×4 unchanged); pixels INSIDE bounds all cleared to (0,0,0,0); pixels OUTSIDE bounds all preserved as fully opaque red (255,0,0,255); source buffer not mutated (proving `_trashPixelsInBox` returns a fresh copy, never in-place). **Part 1 (real UI end to end via real Chromium at 1400×900, 15/15)** — a base64 4×4 magenta PNG fixture opens PictureStudio via `PictureStudio.open(img,{defaultMode:'fill'})`, reaches Edit View via `.picture-studio-cta-secondary`, activates the crop tool via `[data-tile-key='crop']`, then snapshots the crop sub-panel's real DOM into a single probe object BEFORE modal removal (mirroring the established `contextual_collapse_verify.js` discipline where `getComputedStyle` on a removed element silently returns empty strings). Confirms: hint text is the new 'Drag a box around a part of your picture.' verbatim; the action row exists with exactly 2 buttons in Trash → Keep order; Trash It's `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn-danger` class and Keep This's `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn-primary` class both present; both initially `disabled` (no `_cropRect` yet); Undo Trim button present with correct label and `.picture-studio-subpanel-btn-sm` styling, initially disabled; Trash It's computed background is genuinely coral (`rgb(230, 115, 115)`) and text colour is white (proving the new filled-pill CSS took effect); crop tool is genuinely active (`data-active-tool='crop'` on the inner `.picture-studio` root — a real test-methodology bug caught mid-run and disclosed: the initial version queried `data-active-tool` off the outer `.picture-studio-modal`, but `_root` is the inner `.picture-studio` div where the attribute is actually set, fixed by scoping the query correctly); and clicking Trash It with no `_cropRect` is a safe no-op (no throw) — proving the defensive guard `if(!_cropRect||!_workingBuffer) return;` at the top of `_trashCropArea` works. Zero uncaught page errors. Both `goldenBuild.js` suites (World Builder v1 and v2, unaffected — this ship is confined entirely to root Studio's Image Studio modal) PASS unchanged.
